items.title: NTPU AI4X shines at TAAI 2026: AI×ESG paper wins Best Oral Presentation Award, student takes runner-up in Agentic AI competition
items.summary: AI4X Director Prof. Min-Yuh Day chaired TAAI 2026, and cross-disciplinary teams presented three international papers on sustainable finance, smart healthcare, and financial AI. Several NTPU faculty members moderated and spoke at the cross-disciplinary AI sustainability forums.
content: The AI4X Research Center at National Taipei University (NTPU AI4X) delivered strong results at the 31st International Conference on Technologies and Applications of Artificial Intelligence (TAAI 2026). Co-organized by the Taiwanese Association for Artificial Intelligence (TAAI) and NTPU, the conference took place on November 20–21, 2026, at The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort in Sanxia, New Taipei City. AI4X Director Prof. Min-Yuh Day, Professor and Chair of the Graduate Institute of Information Management, served as General Chair.

Under the theme “Agentic AI and Physical AI for Cross-Disciplinary Sustainable Innovation,” TAAI 2026 brought together 450 authors from about 90 institutions in 13 countries and regions. It received 205 submissions and featured 157 paper presentations, alongside keynotes, industry forums, tutorials, and innovation competitions.
[AI×ESG paper wins Best Oral Presentation Award]

Prof. Min-Yuh Day and Wei-Chen Huang, an outstanding NTPU Statistics graduate and member of the AI Aquila R&D team, won the Best Oral Presentation Award in International Oral Session 6 for “Calibrated Hierarchical Structured Decisions for SASB Compliance Evidence in Sustainability Reports” (Paper #209). The study applies AI to assess SASB compliance evidence in corporate sustainability reports, supporting sustainability information governance and corporate transparency.

In smart healthcare, Prof. Day and graduate student Wen-Ze Chen presented “Evidence-Grounded Dental Vision-Language Framework for Implant Detection and Marginal Bone Loss Assessment in Panoramic Radiographs” (Paper #172), applying computer vision and deep learning to dental implant detection and bone loss assessment.

In financial AI, Prof. Day and team members Wei-Hsi Sun, Yi-Ting Liao, and Yi-En Liu presented “Structural Fidelity of Automated Multidimensional AI Judges for Earnings Call Argument Quality Assessment” (Paper #155), examining the trustworthiness of large language models in evaluating argument quality in earnings calls.
[AI CUP talk: ESG commitment verification and Agentic AI]

In the invited session “AI CUP: From AI Competitions to Cross-Disciplinary Innovation and Talent Development,” Prof. Day spoke on “From AI CUP to Agentic AI: Designing and Running the ESG Commitment Verification Competition,” sharing the design, results, and talent development experience of the AI CUP 2026 VeriPromiseESG competition.

The team combined large language models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and multi-agent systems to build VeriPromiseESG4K, a Traditional Chinese dataset of 4,000 annotated sustainability report entries from Taiwan 50 Index constituents across 15 industries. The work has been published at IEEE EM-RITE 2026 and extended through Taiwan–Japan collaboration and the NTCIR-19 international evaluation task.
[NTPU faculty lead the cross-disciplinary AI sustainability forums]

TAAI 2026 featured three Cross-Disciplinary AI Sustainable Innovation Forums, moderated by AI4X Director Prof. Min-Yuh Day, Dean Chia-Ying Chan of the International College of Sustainable Innovation, and Distinguished Prof. Chih-Chien Wang of the Graduate Institute of Information Management. Experts from academia and industry discussed AI in energy governance, sustainable finance, trustworthy AI, environmental regulation, and social innovation.

NTPU speakers included Prof. Haobijam Basanta (Electrical Engineering) on “Beyond Accuracy: Building Trustworthy and Sustainable AI for Real-World Deployment”; Prof. Wei-Lun Chang (Business Administration) on “Sustainable AI Governance: Integrating Environmental Law into the AI Lifecycle”; and Distinguished Prof. Chih-Chien Wang on “Cross-Disciplinary AI and the Digital Divide.” Other speakers covered AI-driven energy governance, financial RAG chatbots, generative AI in legal education, and biotech and health industry transformation.
[Student wins runner-up in NAPAI Agentic AI competition; Assoc. Prof. Pan chairs tutorial and poster session]

First-year master's student Tzu-Wei Hsu, advised by Assoc. Prof. Ling-Yen Pan (Head of the AI4X Education Innovation Division, Graduate Institute of Information Management), won second place in the NAPAI Agentic AI Campus Innovation Competition. Organized by the NAPAI program office, the final and award ceremony were held during TAAI 2026, with 16 teams presenting on site.

On November 21, Assoc. Prof. Pan also chaired “Agentic AI Tutorial 2,” in which Prof. Hao-Chiang Koong Lin of National University of Tainan presented on storyboarding and camera techniques for AI video creation, and co-chaired Domestic Poster Session 4 with Prof. I-Hsien Ting of National University of Kaohsiung, featuring 12 papers on computer vision, multimodal AI, and speech and acoustics.
[Cross-disciplinary teams behind the results]

AI4X works with research teams across NTPU, including the AI Aquila R&D team (co-advised by Distinguished Prof. Chih-Chien Wang and Prof. Min-Yuh Day) and the Intelligent Financial Innovation Technology Lab (IFIT Lab, led by Prof. Day), advancing research in generative AI, intelligent agents, computer vision, ESG analytics, and financial AI.

Launched on August 1, 2026, AI4X connects 64 AI faculty members across NTPU's seven colleges, with three divisions: Industry Technology (Assoc. Prof. Chen-Yu Chiang, Communication Engineering), Cross-Domain Applications (Asst. Prof. Yu-An Lin, Social Work), and Education Innovation (Assoc. Prof. Ling-Yen Pan, Information Management).
[Remarks]

NTPU President Tao-Tung Lin said: “We are honored to co-host TAAI 2026 with the Taiwanese Association for Artificial Intelligence, bringing researchers from 13 countries and regions to Sanxia. NTPU will continue to deepen AI research and talent development, foster cross-disciplinary collaboration, and respond to the needs of industry and society with innovative technology.”

Prof. Min-Yuh Day, AI4X Director and TAAI 2026 General Chair, said: “TAAI 2026 was made possible by 61 organizing committee members from 21 institutions, together with all speakers, researchers, reviewers, session chairs, volunteers, and staff. Beyond 157 papers, the forums on agentic AI, physical AI, industry applications, and sustainability connected research with real-world needs. We hope TAAI continues to expand the international impact of AI research in Taiwan and nurture more cross-disciplinary talent.”

The conference was supported by AI4X administrative specialist Szu-Yin Chen, teaching assistant Ya-Yen Teng of the Graduate Institute of Information Management, Yu-Yu Yeh of the AIAM program, and a cross-disciplinary student team.

items.title: NTPU AI Platform Launch & AI4X Research Center Inauguration Ceremony
items.summary: National Taipei University officially launched its NTPU AI Platform and held the inauguration ceremony for the Advanced Research Center for Cross-Disciplinary AI (AI4X), marking a new stage of AI for every student and every class.
content: On October 1, 2026 (Thursday) at noon, National Taipei University held the "NTPU AI Platform Launch & AI4X Research Center Inauguration Ceremony," announcing the official launch of the university-wide AI platform together with the inauguration of the Advanced Research Center for Cross-Disciplinary AI (AI4X).

Themed "NTPU AI Goes Live - AI for Every Class, AI for Everyone," the event showcased the university's concrete progress in AI teaching and research, bringing together faculty and staff from across the colleges as witnesses.
Program: 12:30 check-in, 12:40 AI platform launch, 13:15 inauguration ceremony, 13:30 close.

organizers: Advanced Research Center for Cross-Disciplinary AI (AI4X), National Taipei University

items.title: CNA coverage: NTPU launches university-wide AI platform for digital equity
items.summary: Central News Agency (CNA) covered the NTPU AI Platform launch and AI4X Research Center inauguration ceremony, featuring remarks from President Lin Tao-Tung, Center Director Min-Yuh Day, and Computer Center Director Chih-Chien Wang on the platform's mission and educational-equity goals.
content: Central News Agency (CNA), via its Global Views China desk, reported on October 1, 2026 that National Taipei University had officially launched its university-wide "NTPU AI Platform," combining open-weight and commercial models to provide free generative AI access to all faculty and students, alongside the inauguration of the Advanced Research Center for Cross-Disciplinary AI (AI4X).

The report quoted President Lin Tao-Tung on how the platform reflects the university's direction of grounding AI innovation in its law, business, and public-affairs strengths; Center Director Min-Yuh Day on AI4X's mission to integrate AI across law, business, public affairs, humanities and social sciences, and sustainability; and Computer Center Director Chih-Chien Wang on how a university-run platform reduces the access gap created by paid commercial AI subscriptions.
The original report is in Chinese; see the CNA link below for the full article.

items.title: NAPAI Agentic AI Campus Innovation Competition
items.summary: College students across Taiwan are invited to solve real campus and field problems with Agentic AI. Entries must be operable, measurable, controllable, and field-verifiable. Online registration closes September 11, 2026; the final takes place on November 21 alongside TAAI 2026.
content: The competition is supervised by the Department of Information and Technology Education, Ministry of Education, organized by the National Agentic & Physical AI Initiative (NAPAI), and co-hosted by the Department of Computer Science and Information Engineering at National Central University and the Graduate Institute of Information Management at National Taipei University, in collaboration with TAAI 2026, the 31st International Conference on Technologies and Applications of Artificial Intelligence.

Teams tackle problems drawn from real campus and field settings using Agentic AI. Entries must be goal-oriented with task decomposition, and meet at least two of the following: tool or external system invocation, state management with dynamic adjustment, and permission and risk control. Results must be operable, measurable, controllable, and field-verifiable.

There are two tracks, a Campus Open Track where teams define their own problem and a Field-Assigned Track based on challenges published by partner organizations. Field themes cover smart academic affairs and learning support, campus administration and service workflows, library and research knowledge services, and industry and public-sector co-creation. Each team registers for one track and one theme.

All currently enrolled college and university students in Taiwan, including master's and doctoral students, are eligible regardless of major. Teams consist of 2 to 5 students, may be cross-school and cross-disciplinary, and may have one faculty advisor.

Key dates: online registration closes Friday, September 11 at 23:59; briefing and capacity-building workshop on Friday, September 18; preliminary submission deadline Friday, October 16; finalists announced Friday, November 6; final and showcase on Saturday, November 21 at The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort in Sanxia, New Taipei City.

Total prize pool is NT$150,000. Each track awards first place NT$25,000, second place NT$15,000, third place NT$10,000, and five honorable mentions of NT$5,000 each. Rules, registration forms, field challenges, and updates are published on the competition website.

items.title: 2026 AI Industry-Academia Development Forum
items.summary: Focused on Agentic AI, industrial AI adoption, innovative applications, and talent development, the forum takes place on October 2, 2026 at National Taipei University of Business, with five keynote speeches and two industry-academia roundtables.
content: As generative AI continues to evolve, artificial intelligence is moving from providing answers toward Agentic AI that understands tasks, plans workflows, coordinates tools, and executes work autonomously. The 2026 AI Industry-Academia Development Forum focuses on four themes: Agentic AI, industrial AI adoption, innovative applications, and talent development.

The morning features five keynote speeches by Yu-Chee Tseng of the Pervasive AI Research Center at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang, Director of AI Research at NVIDIA Taiwan, Chih-Yung Chang of Tamkang University, Chia-Chieh Su, Taiwan Technical Lead at eCloudvalley, and Yang-Ming Han of the Market Intelligence & Consulting Institute (MIC) at the Institute for Information Industry.

Two afternoon roundtables cover AI industry-academia collaboration and practice, and AI talent development and industrial innovation. NTPU Vice President for Research Yu-Hsien Chen speaks on AI in smart healthcare and legal practice in the first roundtable, and NTPU Vice President Yu-Shan Chang chairs the second.

The forum runs from 08:30 to 17:00 on Friday, October 2, 2026 at the International Conference Hall, 10F, Chengxi Building, National Taipei University of Business. It is organized by the Office of Research and Development at NTUB under the Ministry of Education Higher Education Sprout Project. Please refer to the official forum website for the program, speakers, and registration.

items.title: TAAI 2026 — The 31st International Conference on Technologies and Applications of Artificial Intelligence
items.summary: TAAI 2026 will be held on November 20–21, 2026, at The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort in Sanxia, New Taipei City, under the theme “Agentic AI and Physical AI for Cross-Disciplinary Sustainable Innovation.”
content: The 31st International Conference on Technologies and Applications of Artificial Intelligence (TAAI 2026) is jointly organized by the Taiwanese Association for Artificial Intelligence (TAAI) and National Taipei University (NTPU).

The conference theme is “Agentic AI and Physical AI for Cross-Disciplinary Sustainable Innovation,” highlighting autonomous AI agents, embodied intelligence, real-world AI applications, and interdisciplinary sustainable innovation.

TAAI 2026 will take place on November 20–21, 2026, at The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort in Sanxia, New Taipei City. The paper submission deadline is September 14, 2026; please refer to the official conference website for submission, program, and registration details.

items.title: Advanced AI Talent Cultivation Program: Agentic & Physical AI Robotics Curriculum Initiative
items.summary: NAPAI (National Agentic & Physical AI Initiative) focuses on Agentic AI and Physical AI, integrating course co-creation, faculty development, pilot courses, student competitions, and professional communities to cultivate forward-looking AI talent.
content: The Advanced AI Talent Cultivation Program centers on the Agentic & Physical AI Robotics Curriculum Initiative, focusing on the two forward-looking pillars of Agentic AI and Physical AI.

The initiative integrates seed-teacher training, co-creation of course modules, pilot demonstration courses, student hands-on competitions, and community building to strengthen AI education and practical capabilities.
The official website provides news, course resources, community activities, partners, and related learning resources. Please refer to the NAPAI website for the latest information.

items.title: AI4X Research Center officially began operations on August 1, 2026
items.summary: The university-level Advanced Research Center for Cross-Disciplinary AI is now officially operational, with its governance structure in place and first-wave initiatives under way.
content: The Advanced Research Center for Cross-Disciplinary AI (AI4X Research Center), a university-level research center of National Taipei University, has been officially operational since August 1, 2026.

The center connects research strengths in law, business, public affairs, humanities and social sciences, sustainability, and information technology. Its governance structure is in place and the first-wave initiatives are under way; the remaining research, resource, and collaboration mechanisms will be launched in phases.

Center Director: Prof. Min-Yuh Day (Professor & Director, Graduate Institute of Information Management, NTPU). Administrative window: Ms. Szu-Yin Chen, Administrative Specialist (sychen@gm.ntpu.edu.tw, ext. 66977).
organizers: AI4X Research Center, National Taipei University

items.title: AI platforms & teams already in service
items.summary: NTPU AI, the NTPU AI Assistant, and the NTPU AI Aquila Project technical R&D team are now available to the NTPU community.
content: Campus AI platforms and the student technical R&D team are now available to the NTPU community.
NTPU AI: the university AI platform, offering AI conversation, web search, campus search, and file analysis.

NTPU AI Assistant: a smart campus Q&A assistant that brings together administrative, teaching, and learning resources, helping faculty and students find campus information through natural-language questions.
NTPU AI Aquila Project: the technical R&D team, providing technology development, project implementation support, and education & training.
organizers: AI4X Research Center, National Taipei University

content: The center's founding mission (cross-domain research, shared resources, industry-academia collaboration, and responsible AI) and its first-wave work items are now published on this site.

Early work includes cross-college research matchmaking, mapping of on-campus AI research capacity, a management framework for research data and computing resources, cross-domain seed research projects, faculty workshops, and a single window for external collaboration; every item carries its current status and expected timeline.
